title: Wires needed on table to off table.

posts.topic_title: Wires needed on table to off table.
posts.author: Johnfp
posts.post_subject: Wires needed on table to off table.
posts.content_md:
How do you insulate the wires needed to go to devices on table to devices of table? Like the wire from the LCD to the laptop. It's long enough but I was thinking on hanging it on a very loose spring from the ceiling to absorb some movement energy from off the table and through it.

Any other techniques?

posts.topic_title: Wires needed on table to off table.
posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.post_subject: Wires needed on table to off table.
posts.content_md:
It's just not really a problem. Hang it from the ceiling down to the table. No springs needed. You can even go off the side without issue but then its hard to walk around the table. 

Jeff W

posts.topic_title: Wires needed on table to off table.
posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.post_subject: Wires needed on table to off table.
posts.content_md: I just use regular insulated wire-wrapping wire like they have at Radio Shack. I forget the gauge, but it's very thin wire. Works fine without hanging, it just goes from the transducer mirror mount on my table straight to the fringe-locker. If you check McMaster-Carr, they have even finer wire which is stranded, but I haven't had the need to try it. McMaster-Carr is really an excellent source for all kinds of things (fast, reasonable prices, easy online ordering). No holographer should be without them

posts.topic_title: Wires needed on table to off table.
posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.post_subject: Wires needed on table to off table.
posts.content_md: John, the McMaster wire I was talking about is item number 9511T411 at [http://www.mcmaster.com](http://www.mcmaster.com) (unable to provide a direct link)
